stories.headline: Better HTTP/1 connection reuse
stories.summary: The Go Blog Better HTTP/1 connection reuse Nicholas Husin and Damien Neil 14 October 2026 Take a look at the following function: func getStatus(url string) (int, error) { resp, err := http.Get(url) if err != nil { return 0, err } defer resp.Body.Close() return resp.StatusCode, nil } It sends a GET request to url and returns the HTTP status code. Using HTTP/1 ( GODEBUG=http2client=0 ), calling this function 100 times against index.golang.org takes ~710 milliseconds on Go 1.26 on my machine.
stories.why_it_matters: On Go 1.27, the same program takes ~150 milliseconds. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in developers.
key_points: Problem & Context: The Go Blog Better HTTP/1 connection reuse Nicholas Husin and Damien Neil 14 October 2026 Take a look at the following function: func getStatus(url string) (int, error) { resp, err := http.Get(url) if err != nil { return 0, err } defer resp.Body.Close() return resp.StatusCode, nil } It sends a GET request to url and returns the HTTP status code.

Technical Implementation: That is almost 5 times faster! How is such a drastic performance difference possible? The cost of establishing HTTP connections To understand the difference, consider what happens on the network when we make an HTTP request.
Deployment & Impact: Go’s net/http package supports HTTP/1.0, HTTP/1.1, and HTTP/2.

stories.headline: AWS Weekly Roundup: AWS Lambda Web Functions, Amazon S3 on the Vercel Marketplace, and more (October 19, 2026)
stories.summary: Nothing last week added a new kind of compute. What it did instead was shorten the distance between the code you already have and that code being live.
stories.why_it_matters: AWS Lambda learned to run a plain HTTP server with no adapter in front of it, and Amazon S3 became something you can provision from inside the tool you were already using, without opening the AWS Management Console. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cloud.
key_points: Problem & Context: What it did instead was shorten the distance between the code you already have and that code being live.

Technical Implementation: AWS Lambda learned to run a plain HTTP server with no adapter in front of it, and Amazon S3 became something you can provision from inside the tool you were already using, without opening the AWS Management Console.

Deployment & Impact: Lambda now has three form factors on the same Firecracker isolation, which compose inside one application: Event Functions (the model you already know) for async work, Web Functions for the user-facing layer, and MicroVMs for stateful sandboxes running untrusted code.

stories.headline: Amazon S3 is now available on the Vercel Marketplace and v0 by Vercel
stories.summary: Developers building web and AI applications on Vercel can now add Amazon S3 storage resources directly from the Vercel Marketplace and v0, combining the durability, scalability, and performance of S3 with the convenience of Vercel’s provisioning workflow. Starting today, Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) , including Amazon S3 Tables and Amazon S3 Vectors , is natively available on the Vercel Marketplace and v0 by Vercel , covering three distinct workloads: everyday storage, analytics, and AI.

stories.headline: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization
stories.summary: When we previously blogged about our AI code reviewer in April , an average review cost a palatable $1.19. By the end of August, that figure had shot up to about $2.46.
stories.why_it_matters: We hadn't made any significant architectural changes: the coordinator was still handing work to the same set of specialist reviewers, and the same risk tiers decided how intensive of a review we gave. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cloud.
key_points: Problem & Context: When we previously blogged about our AI code reviewer in April , an average review cost a palatable $1.19.
Technical Implementation: With code quality at high effort, the average review now costs just $0.77, down 68% from the $2.43 it averaged over our two most expensive weeks before we started.
Deployment & Impact: About 40% of the savings came from changes and optimizations to the reviewer's code, and the rest from experimenting with which models we use and how much effort they put in.
